In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: For a fixed framework passing bottleneck (lsd_f), adsorbates with a larger heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) experience stronger geometric confinement and therefore a larger entropy loss on adsorption (Sgas - Sads)/R; conversely, for a fixed adsorbate, frameworks with a larger passing free-sphere bottleneck permit more retained configurational freedom and thus smaller entropy loss. The log damping keeps the descriptor finite and comparable across the training support.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: Reported zeolite comparisons (E02, cavity_rotation) associate smaller cavity diameters with larger rotational entropy loss, and E03/E04 indicate both translational and rotational entropy losses grow with confinement. GeDi is a heavy-atom maximum pair distance proxy for molecular length; lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df passing-bottleneck free sphere, which is NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the included-along-path sphere Dif. Using lsd_f assumes that confinement relevant to entropy loss correlates with the tightest passage the molecule must negotiate, an unverified mapping stated as an assumption, not a measured causal quantity. The ratio GeDi/lsd_f is dimensionless, satisfying the log-argument rule; GeDi = 0 for single-site adsorbates is a legitimate physical zero giving descriptor value 0, and lsd_f > 0 on the full training support (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the expression is finite everywhere in-domain. The conditional mechanism cards permit lsd_f and GeDi as proxies only under explicit assumptions (C2, C6), and no source coefficient is imported.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R does not increase with GeDi at fixed lsd_f, or does not decrease with lsd_f at fixed GeDi, in held-out data. A competing explanation is that entropy loss is governed by the included cavity volume along the free path (lsd_p) or by accessible specific volume (AV) rather than by the passing bottleneck; if lsd_p- or AV-based descriptors dominate while GeDi/lsd_f adds no conditional information, this descriptor is redundant and rejected. Additional boundary check: adsorbates with GeDi well below lsd_f still show nonzero confinement loss (e.g., via translational constraints), which the pure bottleneck-passage ratio cannot capture; systematic residuals for such pairs would falsify the mechanism.
proxy_assumptions: GeDi (heavy-atom implicit-H representation) proxies the molecular length scale governing confinement; it is not the full all-atom geometry and is exactly 0 for single-site adsorbates.

lsd_f (Df) proxies the confinement-relevant pore dimension; it is the passing bottleneck, not the global cavity diameter Di and not Dif, so the mapping from the reported FER/FAU cavity-diameter relation (E02) to Df is a hypothesis.
The ratio GeDi/lsd_f measures relative geometric frustration; it does not assert that a threshold ratio 1 corresponds to a physical passage/no-passage event.

final_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: at fixed framework conditions, the entropy loss over R, (Sgas - Sads)/R, increases with the squared ratio of the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) to the framework's largest freely passing sphere diameter (lsd_f, Zeo++ Df). Mechanism: when the molecule's spanned length is comparable to or larger than the bottleneck-crossing free sphere, both translational freedom along the channel network and rotational freedom of elongated guests are more strongly hindered, increasing the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost on adsorption. This transfers the reported cavity-size/confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04: smaller-pore MFI/FER show larger rotational entropy loss than large-pore FAU) to a per-pair geometric proxy, using the bottleneck Df — not a global cavity diameter — as the confinement length.
final_candidate.rationale: Proxy limitations and mechanism: GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance, not a full all-atom molecular cross-section or a rotating-body dimension; lsd_f (Df) is a spherical-probe bottleneck along a periodic free path, not the global cavity diameter Di and not the included-along-path Dif. Neither quantity measures lost degrees of freedom directly; the ratio is a geometric proxy for steric confinement of the guest relative to the narrowest passage. The square keeps the descriptor dimensionless, monotone in both inputs, and emphasizes pairs near the confinement regime where the ratio approaches or exceeds 1 — noting explicitly that ratio = 1 is a chosen reference point of the proxy, not an established physical jamming threshold, since Df is computed for a spherical probe and the adsorbate geometry is heavy-atom implicit-H. The mechanism family couples adsorbate shape with framework connectivity (bottleneck-controlled transport/access geometry), consistent with the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy-loss picture (E03).
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: Falsified if: (1) within the finite training support the entropy loss is flat or decreasing in GeDi/lsd_f at fixed other inputs, i.e., the confinement-ratio direction is wrong; (2) the apparent relation disappears when controlling for probe-accessible volume (AV) or surface area (ASA), indicating the descriptor merely proxies overall pore volume rather than bottleneck confinement (competing explanation); (3) single-site/small adsorbates with legitimate GeDi = 0 (54 training cases, descriptor = 0) systematically show above-average entropy loss, which would break the monotone confinement interpretation; (4) the relation holds only when Df is replaced by Dif, showing the bottleneck role was misassigned (Df is the passing bottleneck; Dif is included-along-path and must not be conflated with it).
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Explicit assumptions, not established causality: (a) the heavy-atom pair distance GeDi adequately represents the adsorbate's confinement-relevant length despite the implicit-H representation; (b) the free-sphere bottleneck Df adequately represents the confinement-relevant framework length, transferring the reported cavity-diameter confinement picture (FER vs FAU) to a bottleneck quantity; (c) the source comparisons (MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, linear alkanes) transfer to this benchmark's molecule-framework pairs at its regime; (d) ratio = 1 is a proxy reference, not a physical equality threshold; (e) no outcome-fitted coefficient is embedded — the descriptor is a pure dimensionless geometric ratio.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support preserved: lsd_f is strictly positive over training (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the division never divides by zero and the ratio is finite for all training rows. GeDi has legitimate physical zeros (54 single-site cases); these map to descriptor value 0 — a valid native value, not missing data — and are not median-imputed. The descriptor is nonnegative and unbounded above only in the extrapolation limit; within training, GeDi <= 10.97181443 angstrom and lsd_f >= 0.85684 angstrom bound the ratio.

However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. draft.name: h1_span_bottleneck_confinement_ratio
draft.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: at fixed framework conditions, the entropy loss over R, (Sgas - Sads)/R, increases with the squared ratio of the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) to the framework's largest freely passing sphere diameter (lsd_f, Zeo++ Df). Mechanism: when the molecule's spanned length is comparable to or larger than the bottleneck-crossing free sphere, both translational freedom along the channel network and rotational freedom of elongated guests are more strongly hindered, increasing the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost on adsorption. This transfers the reported cavity-size/confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04: smaller-pore MFI/FER show larger rotational entropy loss than large-pore FAU) to a per-pair geometric proxy, using the bottleneck Df — not a global cavity diameter — as the confinement length.
draft.rationale: Proxy limitations and mechanism: GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance, not a full all-atom molecular cross-section or a rotating-body dimension; lsd_f (Df) is a spherical-probe bottleneck along a periodic free path, not the global cavity diameter Di and not the included-along-path Dif. Neither quantity measures lost degrees of freedom directly; the ratio is a geometric proxy for steric confinement of the guest relative to the narrowest passage. The square keeps the descriptor dimensionless, monotone in both inputs, and emphasizes pairs near the confinement regime where the ratio approaches or exceeds 1 — noting explicitly that ratio = 1 is a chosen reference point of the proxy, not an established physical jamming threshold, since Df is computed for a spherical probe and the adsorbate geometry is heavy-atom implicit-H. The mechanism family couples adsorbate shape with framework connectivity (bottleneck-controlled transport/access geometry), consistent with the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy-loss picture (E03).
draft.falsification_criteria: Falsified if: (1) within the finite training support the entropy loss is flat or decreasing in GeDi/lsd_f at fixed other inputs, i.e., the confinement-ratio direction is wrong; (2) the apparent relation disappears when controlling for probe-accessible volume (AV) or surface area (ASA), indicating the descriptor merely proxies overall pore volume rather than bottleneck confinement (competing explanation); (3) single-site/small adsorbates with legitimate GeDi = 0 (54 training cases, descriptor = 0) systematically show above-average entropy loss, which would break the monotone confinement interpretation; (4) the relation holds only when Df is replaced by Dif, showing the bottleneck role was misassigned (Df is the passing bottleneck; Dif is included-along-path and must not be conflated with it).

A length-to-sphere-diameter ratio does not capture whether an elongated molecule physically passes a constriction (cross-section and orientation matter), and the implicit-H representation systematically underestimates the true steric envelope. The draft acknowledges these limits but the mechanism as stated ('spanned length comparable to the bottleneck-crossing free sphere') is not established by the descriptor definitions.

Legitimate GeDi = 0 rows (54 single-site training cases) map to descriptor value 0 under the monotone-increasing interpretation, i.e., 'no confinement hindrance'. A single atom or spherical guest can still experience substantial translational/rotational entropy loss in a narrow bottleneck, so descriptor = 0 does not correspond to zero confinement; the draft's falsification criterion (3) is a reasonable test, but the descriptor structurally cannot represent confinement for these rows.

draft.name: h1_span_bottleneck_confinement_ratio
draft.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: at fixed framework conditions, the entropy loss over R, (Sgas - Sads)/R, increases with the squared ratio of the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) to the framework's largest freely passing sphere diameter (lsd_f, Zeo++ Df). Mechanism: when the molecule's spanned length is comparable to or larger than the bottleneck-crossing free sphere, both translational freedom along the channel network and rotational freedom of elongated guests are more strongly hindered, increasing the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost on adsorption. This transfers the reported cavity-size/confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04: smaller-pore MFI/FER show larger rotational entropy loss than large-pore FAU) to a per-pair geometric proxy, using the bottleneck Df — not a global cavity diameter — as the confinement length.
draft.rationale: Proxy limitations and mechanism: GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance, not a full all-atom molecular cross-section or a rotating-body dimension; lsd_f (Df) is a spherical-probe bottleneck along a periodic free path, not the global cavity diameter Di and not the included-along-path Dif. Neither quantity measures lost degrees of freedom directly; the ratio is a geometric proxy for steric confinement of the guest relative to the narrowest passage. The square keeps the descriptor dimensionless, monotone in both inputs, and emphasizes pairs near the confinement regime where the ratio approaches or exceeds 1 — noting explicitly that ratio = 1 is a chosen reference point of the proxy, not an established physical jamming threshold, since Df is computed for a spherical probe and the adsorbate geometry is heavy-atom implicit-H. The mechanism family couples adsorbate shape with framework connectivity (bottleneck-controlled transport/access geometry), consistent with the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy-loss picture (E03).
draft.falsification_criteria: Falsified if: (1) within the finite training support the entropy loss is flat or decreasing in GeDi/lsd_f at fixed other inputs, i.e., the confinement-ratio direction is wrong; (2) the apparent relation disappears when controlling for probe-accessible volume (AV) or surface area (ASA), indicating the descriptor merely proxies overall pore volume rather than bottleneck confinement (competing explanation); (3) single-site/small adsorbates with legitimate GeDi = 0 (54 training cases, descriptor = 0) systematically show above-average entropy loss, which would break the monotone confinement interpretation; (4) the relation holds only when Df is replaced by Dif, showing the bottleneck role was misassigned (Df is the passing bottleneck; Dif is included-along-path and must not be conflated with it).

review_issues.explanation: Quantity mismatch between source and proxy: E02 explicitly identifies the 'average cavity diameter' as the confinement descriptor in the FER/FAU comparison, and source_conditions.C2 states that cavity diameter and lsd_f/lsd_p are different geometric quantities whose proxy mapping must be justified. The draft substitutes the bottleneck free-sphere diameter Df (lsd_f) for the source's cavity diameter without an independently verified mapping; the transfer from cavity-size confinement to bottleneck confinement is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated relation.

Geometric role mismatch inside the ratio: GeDi is the largest heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance — a 1-D molecular length — while lsd_f is a spherical-probe bottleneck diameter along a periodic free path. A length-to-sphere-diameter ratio does not capture whether an elongated molecule physically passes a constriction (cross-section and orientation matter), and the implicit-H representation systematically underestimates the true steric envelope. The draft acknowledges these limits but the mechanism as stated ('spanned length comparable to the bottleneck-crossing free sphere') is not established by the descriptor definitions.

Draft hypothesis claims the ratio proxies BOTH translational and rotational entropy loss, but no rotational proxy (PMI1/PMI2/PMI3, PBF) is used; a single heavy-atom pair distance cannot represent rotational freedom of the guest. The rotational confinement part of the mechanism is asserted rather than represented by any mapped input.

Legitimate GeDi = 0 rows (54 single-site training cases) map to descriptor value 0 under the monotone-increasing interpretation, i.e., 'no confinement hindrance'. A single atom or spherical guest can still experience substantial translational/rotational entropy loss in a narrow bottleneck, so descriptor = 0 does not correspond to zero confinement; the draft's falsification criterion (3) is a reasonable test, but the descriptor structurally cannot represent confinement for these rows.

All four cited comparisons (E01, E02, E04: MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, linear alkanes) have unresolved temperature, loading, and framework chemistry in the excerpts, and source_conditions.C1/C2/C4 mark transfer to this benchmark as hypothetical. The source-specific percentages (e.g., 38% vs 20%) are correctly not embedded, but the directional transfer of the confinement picture to arbitrary molecule-framework pairs at the benchmark regime remains unverified.

Threshold semantics: ratio = 1 is treated in the rationale as a reference point near a 'confinement regime', but GeDi/lsd_f = 1 compares a heavy-atom pair distance to a spherical-probe passing diameter — different geometric quantities — so the value 1 has no demonstrated physical meaning (no established jamming or fit threshold). The draft flags this, but the squared emphasis 'near the confinement regime where the ratio approaches or exceeds 1' still implies physical significance for that value.

The squared ratio is monotone in both inputs, but the proposed conditional prediction (increase GeDi at fixed lsd_f → loss increases) embeds the assumption that larger molecular span always means more confinement for a fixed bottleneck. For very large molecules relative to the bottleneck, adsorption location or excluded configurations could change non-monotonically; the monotone form is an empirical choice, not a derived result, and this is not stated as an explicit limit in the boundary description.

The execution_check rejection reason 'Wrong physical variable mapping: GeDi requires heavy_atom_pair_distance' is inconsistent with the draft's own variable_mappings, which already assigns GeDi to heavy_atom_pair_distance. The actual grounds for rejection are unresolved in the record; this inconsistency is unknown and should be resolved rather than treated as a confirmed definition error or dismissed.

Falsification criterion (2) uses AV/ASA as controls for 'overall pore volume', but AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and AV = 0 does not imply zero physical adsorption space; using AV as a controlling covariate inherits that definition limitation. Absent knowledge of framework-connectivity effects (no graph edges available for the bottleneck-transport mechanism family in this record) is unknown and does not disprove the proposed mechanism.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. appended.name: h1_span_bottleneck_confinement_ratio
appended.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: at fixed framework conditions, the entropy loss over R, (Sgas - Sads)/R, increases with the squared ratio of the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) to the framework's largest freely passing sphere diameter (lsd_f, Zeo++ Df). Mechanism: when the molecule's spanned length is comparable to or larger than the bottleneck-crossing free sphere, both translational freedom along the channel network and rotational freedom of elongated guests are more strongly hindered, increasing the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost on adsorption. This transfers the reported cavity-size/confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04: smaller-pore MFI/FER show larger rotational entropy loss than large-pore FAU) to a per-pair geometric proxy, using the bottleneck Df — not a global cavity diameter — as the confinement length.
appended.rationale: Proxy limitations and mechanism: GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance, not a full all-atom molecular cross-section or a rotating-body dimension; lsd_f (Df) is a spherical-probe bottleneck along a periodic free path, not the global cavity diameter Di and not the included-along-path Dif. Neither quantity measures lost degrees of freedom directly; the ratio is a geometric proxy for steric confinement of the guest relative to the narrowest passage. The square keeps the descriptor dimensionless, monotone in both inputs, and emphasizes pairs near the confinement regime where the ratio approaches or exceeds 1 — noting explicitly that ratio = 1 is a chosen reference point of the proxy, not an established physical jamming threshold, since Df is computed for a spherical probe and the adsorbate geometry is heavy-atom implicit-H. The mechanism family couples adsorbate shape with framework connectivity (bottleneck-controlled transport/access geometry), consistent with the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy-loss picture (E03).
appended.falsification_criteria: Falsified if: (1) within the finite training support the entropy loss is flat or decreasing in GeDi/lsd_f at fixed other inputs, i.e., the confinement-ratio direction is wrong; (2) the apparent relation disappears when controlling for probe-accessible volume (AV) or surface area (ASA), indicating the descriptor merely proxies overall pore volume rather than bottleneck confinement (competing explanation); (3) single-site/small adsorbates with legitimate GeDi = 0 (54 training cases, descriptor = 0) systematically show above-average entropy loss, which would break the monotone confinement interpretation; (4) the relation holds only when Df is replaced by Dif, showing the bottleneck role was misassigned (Df is the passing bottleneck; Dif is included-along-path and must not be conflated with it).
appended.proxy_assumptions: Explicit assumptions, not established causality: (a) the heavy-atom pair distance GeDi adequately represents the adsorbate's confinement-relevant length despite the implicit-H representation; (b) the free-sphere bottleneck Df adequately represents the confinement-relevant framework length, transferring the reported cavity-diameter confinement picture (FER vs FAU) to a bottleneck quantity; (c) the source comparisons (MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, linear alkanes) transfer to this benchmark's molecule-framework pairs at its regime; (d) ratio = 1 is a proxy reference, not a physical equality threshold; (e) no outcome-fitted coefficient is embedded — the descriptor is a pure dimensionless geometric ratio.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support preserved: lsd_f is strictly positive over training (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the division never divides by zero and the ratio is finite for all training rows. GeDi has legitimate physical zeros (54 single-site cases); these map to descriptor value 0 — a valid native value, not missing data — and are not median-imputed. The descriptor is nonnegative and unbounded above only in the extrapolation limit; within training, GeDi <= 10.97181443 angstrom and lsd_f >= 0.85684 angstrom bound the ratio.
